title: A rose made of galaxies
caption: The interacting galaxies Arp 273, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Arp 273 · constellation Andromeda · about 300 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble image shows Arp 273, a pair of galaxies caught interacting. The larger of the two has a distorted shape, bearing clear signs of tidal interactions with its smaller companion.

Tidal interactions happen when galaxies pass close enough for gravity to pull unevenly on them, stretching and bending their structure. In this case astronomers think the encounter was more intimate than a close pass, and the smaller galaxy is thought to have actually passed through the larger one. Galaxies are mostly empty space between their stars, so such a crossing does not mean stars smash together, but it can badly disturb the shape of both galaxies.
The release celebrated 21 years since Hubble was launched. The pair lies about 300 million light-years away in the constellation Andromeda.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.63 x 2.66 arcminutes) and distance (300 million light years), the frame spans roughly 230,000 × 232,000 light-years. Its light set out about 300 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using filters in ultraviolet, blue and red light. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of the data is ultraviolet light, which the eye cannot see, and the pair is far too faint to see this way without a large telescope.
